headline: Mechanical and diffusive mechanisms in silico generate emergent tissue geometry
label: Mechanical Tissue Morphogenesis Modelling
summary: Recent preprints couple explicit physical mechanisms to emergent geometry, with connectivity and stress signals evolving during growth.
synthesis: The shared thread is an explicit physical mechanism, mechanical or diffusive, that generates biological geometry in simulation. A coupled vertex-flow model attributes lumen formation, budding, and branching to hyaluronic acid osmotic pressure in intercellular space, and a 3D cell-fiber model reproduces adipose tissue architectures and heterogeneity. A two-stage diffusion-driven model reproduces diatom silica rib branching and pore formation on a finite element mesh. A topoietic stress-signal model, calibrated to Xenopus group data, reproduces cross-embryo rescue rates. A focal adhesion-actomyosin model adds a molecular layer, with ECM stiffness history steering adhesion mode selection. What is new is the explicit linkage of mechanism to emergent geometry, with connectivity changing during growth. Items are preprints describing model-based reproduction rather than experimental comparison.
